notes.overview: Fuji is a 4.56 km, 16-corner lap built around one of the longest main straights in racing, so the exits onto straights are worth more than straight-line drag savings. The lap splits into a fast first half (the Turn 1 stop, Turn 3 and the 100R right-hander), a hairpin and flat-out 300R section, then the slow, twisty final sector ending at Panasonic Corner. It is hard on rear tyres through the repeated slow traction zones, and brake temperatures climb quickly if you brake too aggressively. Stability under braking matters more than rotation; the classic mistakes are overdriving Turn 1, getting on the throttle too soon at the slow corners, and leaning on the kerbs too much in the last sector.

corners.1: The end of the main straight and one of the biggest stops on the calendar. Do all the braking in a straight line and do not carry deep trail braking into the turn; in a Hypercar, lean on the ABS while keeping the car aerodynamically loaded. Most cars take it in second gear. Put traction first and focus on a clean exit.
corners.3: Quick left-hander. If it needs braking, the marker is roughly 80 m; third or fourth gear. Hit the apex precisely and use all of the road and the kerb on the way out, but running wide costs downforce and exit speed in a Hypercar. Finish settled in the middle of the track to set up 100R.
corners.4-5: 100R: a long right-hander that keeps tightening into Turn 5. Turning in early leaves you fighting understeer all the way round, so hold off and take a late apex, and be patient with the throttle. Keep the steering smooth to protect the front tyres. Hypercars may need a small lift just after the painted marking on the right-hand side.
corners.6-7: The slow left-hand hairpin. Brake in a straight line only, get the car turned before you pick up the throttle (Hypercars can help rotate it with throttle modulation), and feed the power in gently: too much too soon overheats the rear tyres. Set up the exit for the fast section that follows.
corners.8-9: Turn 8 and 300R are fast right-handers taken flat out. Use as little steering as possible to keep drag and aero disruption down; in a Hypercar keep the car stable on exit under all that torque.
corners.10-11: Dunlop, the slow chicane. The inside kerb can be attacked hard in a GT3, but in a stiffly sprung Hypercar a heavy hit can unsettle the car, so be more careful. Getting on the throttle early out of Turn 11 is what carries speed through the middle of the sector.
corners.12: Flat-out kink after the chicane. Cut a little of the inside kerb (lightly in a Hypercar), keep the car stable, and move to the left side of the track ready for the final sector.
corners.13: Fast, flowing right-hander that needs commitment. Keep the steering steady: every correction scrubs a lot of speed. Aim for a mid-to-late apex and do not let it run wide on exit.
corners.14-15: Medium-speed double left. Brake on a diagonal line, from the left side for Turn 14 across toward the right for Turn 15. Entry speed is the priority; the guide gives an early-to-mid apex for GT3 and mid-to-late for Hypercar. Do not run wide, and finish on the left ready for Panasonic Corner.
corners.16: Panasonic Corner, the most important corner for lap time because it opens onto the main straight. Brake in a straight line from the left side, use only the flat kerbs, and take a late apex so exit speed and traction come first.
